foodDescription: Small grilled sausages of minced beef, ten to a portion, in a soft somun flatbread with raw onion. Sometimes with kajmak, a rich clotted cream.
Thin pastry rolled around minced meat and baked in a spiral. In Bosnia only the meat version is burek. The others are just called pita.
The other pitas: zeljanica is filled with spinach and cheese, sirnica with cheese alone, and krompiruša with potato.
A round, puffy flatbread with a crosshatched top, baked fresh in Sarajevo bakeries. During Ramadan a special version is sold at sunset.
A creamy chicken and okra soup, named after the Ottoman beys, the local lords, who are said to have favored it.
Small dumplings filled with minced meat, served with a garlic yogurt sauce and red pepper butter.
Whole onions hollowed out and stuffed with minced meat and rice, cooked in a sour sauce. A Sarajevo specialty.
A whole apple poached in sugar syrup, stuffed with walnuts, and topped with whipped cream. An Ottoman dessert.
Layers of thin pastry with walnuts, soaked in syrup. Sold by the piece in the slastičarnas, the sweet shops of Baščaršija.
Finely ground coffee boiled in a small copper pot called a džezva, poured into tiny cups, and drunk slowly with a sugar cube and Turkish delight.
Beer from the Sarajevo brewery, founded in 1864. Its spring supplied the city with water during the siege.
Strong fruit brandy, most often from plums (šljivovica). Offered to guests and drunk in small glasses.
